svg.title: Earlier global-ring reference with direct pump-band coefficient access
svg.desc: Synchronized parallel fiber loops retain separate coefficient frames for every layer, head and Monarch bank. Each bank frame has R time slots, each carrying the complete 2K minus 1 frequency coefficient comb. A shared two-bank optical processor taps the selected frame and later injects its optical update into the matching returning slot. A known reference comb with selectable phase ramps supplies fixed partners. Temporary optical key, error and accumulator buffers are separate from recurrent memory. Detected head outputs stream into a digital projection accumulator, then wait at an all-head barrier before normalization, MLP and next-layer input encoding. A conservative schedule predicts on lap r, writes on lap r plus jW and reads the query on lap r plus jW plus jQ. Other frames bypass the update, and a next-layer start requires both ready inputs and an available memory frame. A guard interval never stops circulation or eliminates multi-pass timing and loss.

g.text: Earlier global-ring reference: heads and layers share one optical engine
Current direction uses separate layer modules. This reference retains the conservative later-lap access schedule.
PERSISTENT MEMORY — n synchronized fiber lanes
Temporal address: (layer p, head h, bank ℓ, partner slot m). Spatial lane f and coefficient frequency s are not serialized here.
Each slot contains the full 2K−1-line coefficient comb. This is frame order, not a one-pass execution schedule.
Unselected frames bypass update. Apply the model’s forgetting gate once per token update; extra laps add physical loss.
Known reference comb + spectral phase-ramp selector
Same calibrated bₘ for prediction, gradient and query sweeps
Reuse across heads and layers; n spatial lanes in parallel
Local optical residuals → full SFG coefficient updates
Inject Δa directly in the pump band
Inject only when its original slot returns
Key / query replay and bank-1 output
Completed residual replay across R slots
Separate lifetimes and resets from memory.
Time gradient generation to match write slots.
q, k, v and gate maps
Digital work streams while later heads run. Dense cross-head mixing and nonlinearities leave a final dependency after head H.
A scheduler aligns frame address, pass type, reference phase, optical replay and injection; unready frames circulate on bypass.
Sharing the processor changes timing and resources, not the independent recurrent state assigned to each layer–head pair.
CONSERVATIVE SERVICE SCHEDULE — one selected bank frame
jW and jQ are positive integer lap offsets set by latency; this is a causal schedule assuming adequate optical retention.
Tap all R old-state slots with key k
Replay k, e and matching bₘ
Generate / align Δa; inject into all R slots
Finish bank 1 before its shuffled output supplies bank 2. Finish bank 2 before emitting that head’s digital output.
The logical inter-layer gap ends only when both next-layer inputs and the required coefficient frame are available.
What the recirculating-memory design must establish
Round-trip time and frame packing · residual and write latency · buffer lifetimes · head-service order · digital-tail budget
Per-lap attenuation / phase / noise · calibrated read taps and coherent injection · loss during skipped frames and extra laps
Functional proposal, not fabrication geometry. Guard intervals consume loop duration; they do not by themselves guarantee timing closure or memory fidelity.
